title: Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMC) and plasma isolation from whole peripheral blood
author: Jennifer L. Dembinski

steps_raw.instruction: Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMC) and plasma isolation from whole peripheral blood
Miloje Savic and Jennifer L. Dembinski
Infection Control and Environmental Health, Norwegian Institute of Public Health, Oslo, Norway

This protocol describes isolation of PBMC from human whole peripheral blood samples by density gradient centrifugation, using One SepMate-50ml tube (https://www.stemcell.com/sepmate-trade-hassle-free-pbmcs-in-just-15-minutes.html), followed by freeze and thaw protocol.
SepMate 50ml tubes (https://www.stemcell.com/products/brands/sepmate.html)
Density gradient medium (Lymphoprep/Ficoll)
Peripheral blood sample collection tubes (ACD/yellow top tubes)
Sterile pipettes and disposable tips
AIM-V medium (ThermoFisher Scientific)
-80˚C and -150˚C freezer
Important: Work under sterile conditions, ideally in a laminar flow class II biosafety cabinet
Ensure that the sample, saline, density gradient medium and centrifuge are all at room temperature (15 - 25°C).

Add 15 mL of density gradient medium (e.g. Ficoll, Sigma-Aldrich) to the SepMate-50 tube by carefully pipetting it through the central hole of the SepMate-50 insert. The top of the density gradient medium will be above the insert.
Important: Small bubbles may be present in the density gradient medium after pipetting. This will not affect SepMate performance.
Dilute the blood sample with an equal volume of saline in a separate 50ml tube. Mix gently.
Keeping the SepMate-50 tube vertical, add the diluted sample by pipetting it down the side of the SepMate-50 tube. The sample will mix with the density gradient medium above the insert.
Centrifuge at 1200 x g for 10 minutes at room-temperature (15 - 25°C), with the brake on.
Using a pipette, collect 3ml plasma from the very top layer of the SepMate-50 tube. Aliquot to 1ml per cryovial tube and store at -20°C.
Pour off the top layer of the SepMate-50 tube, which contains the enriched PBMCs, into a new 50ml tube. Do not hold the SepMate-50 tube in the inverted position for longer than 5 seconds.
Fill up the 50ml tube with the enriched PBMCs with warm AIM-V media, centrifuge at 1200 x g for 10 minutes. Repeat procedure 2 times to remove all Ficoll solution.

Resuspend the cell pellet in 1ml AIM-V media, count PBMC, adjust volume to 5 million cells/ml freezing media (see Freeze and Thaw Protocol bellow), and slowly freeze cells at -80°C by using 1°C/min cooling rate for successful cryopreservation (e.g. use Mr. Frosty freezing container). Next day transfer vials to -150°C freezer for long-term storage.
For more details see Stemcell Sepmate Protocol:
http://www.stemcell.com/~/media/Technical%20Resources/6/D/4/9/D/29251PIS_2_0_0.pdf
https://cdn.stemcell.com/media/files/pis/29251-PIS_2_0_0.pdf
Freeze and Thaw Protocol
Important: Work under sterile conditions, ideally in a laminar flow class II biosafety cabinet.
Prepare freeze medium (65% AIM-V, 25%FBS, 10% DMSO). Label cryogenic vials with date, cell type, and user’s initials.
Suction away supernatant from centrifuged PBMC (following the procedure described above) and add freeze medium. Triturate cells until homogeneous.
Quickly aliquot 1 mL of cells in freeze medium per cryogenic vial. Screw each vial closed.
Put vials into Mr.Frosty freezing container, and leave at –80°C freezer.
Next day, transfer cell vials into appropriate rack in liquid N2 tank, or -150°C freezer.
Rapidly thaw cell vial in 37°C water bath until only a small ice pellet remains. Spray down vial with 70% ethanol, wipe, and place into a laminar flow class II biosafety cabinet.
Pipet contents of vial (~ 1 mL) into T15ml tube.
Slowly add 10 mL of prewarmed AIM-V medium.

Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature. Remove the supernatant, resuspend cells in fresh 10ml AIM-V, centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature, and remove the supernatant. Resuspend cells in 1ml of AIM-V and count the cells.
Adjust cell count per ml of media according to desired downstream protocol (e.g. ELISpot, flow cytometry, in vitro assays etc).
